RE: Hernandez v. L.A. Care Health Plan (L.A.S.C. 26AVSC00192) [LMR-8864]

Bill Seldeen
to me, Felix
Thu, May 14, 3:27 PM (2 days ago)

Dear Mr. Hernandez,

I write in advance of the small claims hearing next week. I have completed a preliminary review of the file, and I wanted to share some information that may be helpful to you as you prepare. My intention is simply to explain a few legal issues that may affect your case and to ask that you reconsider whether to discuss a resolution of the matter to save the Court and L.A. Care staff’s time.

First, as you know, L.A. Care is a public agency. Under the California Government Claims Act, anyone who wants to sue a public agency for money damages must first submit a written government claim directly to the agency, and it is the burden of the plaintiff to demonstrate compliance. This process gives the agency an opportunity to review and respond before a lawsuit is filed. At this time, we have no record that you submitted a government claim to L.A. Care. Your March 26 complaint to the Department of Manage Health Care does not meet this requirement. If you believe you complied with the presentation requirement, please send me a copy, otherwise we will need to bring this issue to the court’s attention.

Second, your small claims complaint cites the Knox-Keene Act. The Knox-Keene Act does not include what is called "private right of action," meaning the statute does not allow an individual person to sue directly under that law. Because of this, the court is not able to grant the type of relief you are requesting based on the Knox-Keene Act.

Third, it appears that L.A. Care is not the correct party for the issue you are raising. Pharmacy benefits for Medi-Cal members are handled by Medi-Cal Rx, a separate program administered by the State of California. L.A. Care does not make pharmacy coverage decisions or process pharmacy claims in this program. More information about Medi-Cal Rx is available at https://medi-calrx.dhcs.ca.gov.

I understand your frustration, especially when you are trying to resolve an issue and are directed to different entities. L.A. Care’s mission is to provide high-quality, accessible health care to our members and to support the health needs of Los Angeles County communities. When time and resources are spent on matters that cannot be legally resolved through the courts, it takes attention away from the services we work to provide for all members.

If you would like to discuss any of this by phone or email, I remain available.

Best regards,

Bill Seldeen

Nicolas Hernandez
